summary: No region-specific signal for Cusco was identified in the source inventory: no departmental law or ordinance, no local enforcement practice, no incident series and no local institution. The national assessment for Peru applies.
tangentialFactors:
The three sources that touch on Cusco do so only as an instance of Peru-wide coverage. The 2025 congressional reporting on restrictions on public-restroom access describes a measure of national scope, and the 2020–2023 violence and rights-violation figures are national totals; neither is disaggregated to Cusco or to any other department.

The national homicide and violation counts are raw numbers without a population denominator, so any ranking of Peru against other jurisdictions on those figures would rest on raw counts alone and would not indicate per-capita risk.
localsOnly: No Cusco-specific resident-facing provision was identified: the inventory contains no departmental or municipal rule governing facilities, identity documents, health services or anti-discrimination complaints for people living in the department.
outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved: whether the Cusco regional government or municipal authorities have issued any ordinance on restroom access, anti-discrimination or services for trans residents is not sourced here.

Unresolved: no source documents how police, health facilities or transport hubs in Cusco handle gender-variant presentation, identity documents or complaints, so local enforcement practice cannot be described.

The national monitoring-body report covering 2020–2023 gives totals for Peru as a whole and does not break them down by department, so Cusco's share of those cases is not sourced.
